mainTopic: The end of דוד's question, and the משנה about a fire that crosses a fence, a public road, or a river
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of what דוד asked during the war with the פלשתים. The opinion that he asked about טמון באש is tested against the field verses, "he would not drink it," and "he poured it out to ה׳," and it answers each challenge. Then a new משנה teaches that if a fire crosses a fence four אמות high, a public road, or a river, the one who lit it is פטור. רב פפא settles a ברייתא that seems to disagree: the two sources count toward four אמות from opposite directions. רבא and רב פפא add that in a thorny field the four אמות are measured from the tops of the thorns. רב and שמואל argue about whether the public-road exemption is about a high flame or a low flame, and a ברייתא supports רב. The גמרא says the public-road rule follows רבי אליעזר. רב and שמואל also disagree whether "river" means a real river or a water channel, which matters when it is dry. Finally, a משנה about פאה leads to two definitions of שלולית, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why are the two verses about the fields needed?
steps.stepSummary: According to the view that דוד asked about טמון באש, the פסוקים about a field of lentils and a field of barley seem to serve no purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says דוד was asking about a hidden item burned in a fire, why does he need the verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the opinion of רבא in the name of רב נחמן. If דוד's question was about טמון באש, the פסוקים that mention lentils and barley seem to be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other two opinions use the lentil field and the barley field to explain what דוד asked. If the question was only about טמון באש, those details add nothing. So the challenge is: what do these verses teach under this view?

keyTerms.meaning: But according to the one who says
An item hidden inside something that a fire burns
He was asking / it was his question

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
that he was asking about a hidden item in a fire,
why does he need the verses?
phrases.notes: The two verses are the field of lentils (שמואל ב 23:11) and the field of barley (דברי הימים א 11:13).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טָמוּן בָּאֵשׁ קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ, מַאי אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ קְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the opinions about דוד's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion of רבא in the name of רב נחמן that דוד asked about טמון באש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verses about lentil and barley fields only make sense if the question involved those fields. Under the טמון באש view they seem unneeded.

steps.title: He asked about both
steps.stepSummary: דוד asked about טמון באש and also one of the other two questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say to you: he was asking about a hidden item and also about one of these other questions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opinions do not have to exclude each other. דוד asked about טמון באש and also one of the other questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verses about the fields still teach something, because they back up the second question דוד also asked. The טמון באש view only adds a question. It does not replace the others.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (a defense on behalf of an opinion)

phrases.english: He could say to you:
about a hidden item and one of these
phrases.notes: "These" means the other two questions: burning the barley stacks, or paying back barley with lentils.

phrases.english: he was asking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: טָמוּן וַחֲדָא מֵהָנָךְ קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Combining opinions: דוד asked more than one question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The טמון באש view seemed to leave the field verses unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד asked about טמון באש plus one of the other questions, so the verses are still needed.

steps.title: What does "he would not drink it" mean?
steps.stepSummary: Under the other two views, דוד refused to rely on a permitted but uncomfortable ruling. Under the טמון באש view, the answer was a plain tradition, so why did he refuse?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says one of these two questions, this is what is written: "But he would not drink it". He said: since there is a prohibition involved, it is not acceptable to me. But according to the one who says he asked about a hidden item in a fire: after all, it was a tradition that they sent him. So what does "he would not drink it" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge against the טמון באש view. It uses the words "ולא אבה לשתותם" from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the other views, the ruling allowed a king something that is normally an איסור, so דוד chose not to use it. Under the טמון באש view, the answer was just a received גמרא with nothing troubling in it. Refusing to "drink" it then seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works well (opens a contrast)

steps.confusionAlert: The "water" דוד would not drink is being read as the halachic answer his men brought back, not only as real water.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says these two,
this is what is written:
"But (David) would not drink it"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 23:16. The word in round brackets is not in the פסוק itself, and some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: he said: since there is a prohibition,
it is not acceptable to me.
But according to the one who says
he was asking about a hidden item in a fire,
after all, it was a tradition that they sent him,
what is "(David) would not drink it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge against the same טמון באש view, this time from a different phrase of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Refusing to "drink" only makes sense if the ruling involved something troubling. A plain tradition has nothing to refuse.

steps.title: He did not quote it in their names
steps.stepSummary: "He would not drink it" means דוד refused to repeat the halacha in the names of the men who risked their lives to get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means that he did not say it in their names. He said: this is what I received from the court of שמואל הרמתי: anyone who hands himself over to die for words of Torah, we do not say a matter of הלכה in his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "not drinking" means דוד would not quote the ruling in the names of his men. He explains this with a tradition from the בית דין of שמואל הרמתי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The men broke through the enemy camp to ask the question, putting their lives at risk for Torah. The tradition says such a person is not quoted by name for a halacha. So under this view, "not drinking" is about how the ruling was quoted, not about refusing the ruling itself.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hands himself over to die

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a rule about quoting Torah: someone who put his life in danger for Torah is not quoted by name for a הלכה.

phrases.english: That he did not say it in their names.
phrases.notes: "Their names" means the soldiers who went through the enemy camp to bring back the answer.

phrases.english: He said: this is what I received
from the court of Samuel of Ramah:
anyone who hands himself over to die
for words of Torah,
we do not say a matter of halacha in his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא אַמְרִינְהוּ מִשְּׁמַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Not drinking" seemed to mean refusing to rely on the ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under the טמון באש view, it means refusing to quote the ruling in the names of those who risked their lives.

steps.title: What does "he poured it out to ה׳" mean?
steps.stepSummary: Under the other views, pouring out means acting לשם שמים by not relying on a leniency. Under the טמון באש view, what does it mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: "He poured it out to ה׳". Granted, according to the one who says these two, it is because he acted for the sake of Heaven. But according to the one who says it was about a hidden item in a fire, what does "he poured it out to ה׳" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge to the טמון באש view, this time from the words "ויסך אותם לה׳".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the other views, דוד gave up a leniency that was allowed for a king, and that was an act לשם שמים. Under the טמון באש view there was no leniency to give up. So what was the "pouring out to ה׳"?

phrases.english: "He poured it out to the Lord"
Granted, according to the one who says these two,
it is because he acted for the sake of Heaven.
But according to the one who says a hidden item in a fire,
what is "He poured it out to the Lord"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיַּסֵּךְ אֹתָם לַה׳ – בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge against the טמון באש view, from the next phrase in the same פסוק.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring out "to ה׳" suggests giving up something for Heaven's sake. Under this view there was nothing to give up.

steps.title: He said it in the name of the tradition
steps.stepSummary: "Poured it out to ה׳" means דוד taught the ruling in the name of the tradition, not in any person's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he said it in the name of the tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "pouring out to ה׳" means דוד said the הלכה in the name of the tradition itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes together with step 4. He did not name the soldiers. Instead, he gave the ruling over as a general received tradition, as if handing it to ה׳ rather than to any person.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of the tradition

steps.whatToRemember: The טמון באש view holds up against all three challenges. דוד asked about טמון באש plus another question. He did not quote the soldiers who risked their lives ("would not drink"). He gave the ruling in the name of the tradition ("poured it out to ה׳").

phrases.english: That he said it in the name of the tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַמְרִינְהוּ מִשְּׁמָא דִגְמָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Poured out to ה׳" seemed to mean giving up a leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under the טמון באש view, it means דוד quoted the ruling in the name of the tradition, without naming anyone.

steps.title: The משנה: fire that crosses a tall fence, road, or river
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if a fire crosses a fence four אמות high, a public road, or a river, the one who lit it is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a fire crossed a fence that is four אמות high, or a public road, or a river, and then did damage, the person who lit it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives three barriers that, once a fire jumps over them, free the person who lit it from paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these barriers normally stops a fire. If the fire still got past one of them, the damage on the other side is treated as something the person who lit it could not have expected, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (the main text the גמרא discusses)
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: MISHNA: If it crossed a fence
phrases.notes: "It" is the fire someone lit. The משנה doesn't say the word, but that is the subject.

phrases.english: that is four cubits high,
or a public road, or a river –
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עָבְרָה גָּדֵר שֶׁהוּא גָּבוֹהַּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The earlier discussion about דוד is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fire that crosses a four-אמות fence, a public road, or a river leaves the one who lit it פטור.

steps.title: A teaching that seems to say the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says a fire crossing a four-אמות fence makes the person חייב, which contradicts the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if a fire crossed a fence four אמות high, the person is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that seems to give the opposite ruling for the very same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a four-אמות fence makes him פטור, and the ברייתא says a four-אמות fence makes him חייב. Both talk about exactly four אמות, so they appear to clash directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: But isn't it taught:
if it crossed a fence that is
four cubits high – he is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a four-אמות fence makes him פטור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules חייב in the identical case of a four-אמות fence.

steps.title: Both sources agree: they just count from opposite directions
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה counts down from tall fences to four, and the ברייתא counts up from short fences to four. They do not really disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Our משנה counts from high to low: six אמות, exempt; five אמות, exempt; down to four אמות, exempt. The ברייתא counts from low to high: two אמות, liable; three אמות, liable; up to four אמות, liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the contradiction. Each source is describing a range of fence heights that ends at four, but from opposite ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה starts with tall fences and works down. Everything from four אמות and up is פטור. The ברייתא starts with short fences and works up, listing the liable heights that lead up to four. So "four" in each source marks the edge of a range from a different direction, and there is no real argument.

keyTerms.meaning: "Our תנא", the author of our משנה
"The outside תנא", the author of the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and the ברייתא agree. They describe the same rule by counting from opposite ends, and four אמות is the dividing line.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The tanna of our Mishnah counts
from above to below:
six cubits – exempt,
five cubits – exempt,
down to four cubits – exempt.
The tanna of the outside teaching
phrases.notes: "Outside" means a teaching left outside the משנה, which is the ברייתא.

phrases.english: counts from below to above:
two cubits – liable,
three cubits – liable,
up to four cubits – liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: תַּנָּא דִּידַן קָא חָשֵׁיב מִלְּמַעְלָה לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the wording: the two sources count in opposite directions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה and the ברייתא give opposite rulings for the same four-אמות fence.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה counts down to four (פטור) and the ברייתא counts up toward four (חייב). Both describe one rule from different ends.

steps.title: The four-אמות rule applies even in a field of thorns
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that a four-אמות fence frees the person from paying even when the field is full of thorns.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the four אמות they said makes him exempt applies even in a field of thorns.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new detail to the משנה's rule. It holds even in a thorny field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thorns catch fire easily and can carry flames higher, so you might think a four-אמות fence is not enough there. רבא teaches that the rule does not change: four אמות still makes him פטור.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The four cubits that they said is exempt –
even in a field of thorns.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ דְּפָטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the four-אמות rule is settled, רבא adds how far it reaches.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A four-אמות fence makes him פטור even in a field of thorns.

steps.title: Measure the four אמות from the top of the thorns
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that in a thorny field, the four אמות are counted from the tops of the thorns upward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: and the four אמות are measured from the top edge of the thorns and up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא clarifies רבא's statement. In a thorny field, the fence must rise four אמות above the thorns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thorns themselves can carry the fire upward, so their height does not count toward the four אמות. The fence counts as a real barrier only if it stands four full אמות above the thorns.

keyTerms.meaning: The top edge of the thorns

steps.whatToRemember: A four-אמות fence makes him פטור. In a thorny field, the four אמות are measured above the tops of the thorns.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And from the edge of the thorns and upward
four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּמִשְּׂפַת קוֹצִים וּלְמַעְלָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to measure רבא's rule from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a field of thorns, the four אמות are measured from the tops of the thorns.

steps.title: רב limits the exemption to a high flame
steps.stepSummary: רב says the משנה's exemption only applies to a flame that shoots straight up. A low flame that creeps along the ground makes the person חייב even 100 אמות away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: The משנה only taught this exemption for a flame that shoots up high. But for a flame that bends low, the person is liable even up to a hundred אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that the משנה's exemption only applies to a certain kind of fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flame that shoots upward does not easily travel sideways, so a fence or road can stop it. A flame that bends low creeps along the ground and spreads easily. So for a low flame, the fence or road does not free the person, and he is חייב even far away.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this for... (a phrase that narrows a rule)
A flame that shoots straight up high
A flame that bends low and spreads along the ground
A cubit, a measure of length (about an arm's length)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two flame words closely. קולחת goes UP, and נכפפת bends DOWN. רב and שמואל use the same two words but reach opposite results, so it is easy to mix them up.

phrases.english: Rav says:
They taught this only for a flame that shoots up high,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that a fire crossing a public road makes him פטור.

phrases.english: but for a flame that bends low,
he is liable even up to a hundred cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּקוֹלַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 7 and narrows the case in which its exemption applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption applies only to a high flame. With a low flame the person is liable even up to 100 אמות.

steps.title: שמואל says the משנה is about a low flame
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the משנה is talking about a low flame. With a high flame, even the smallest gap makes the person פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says: Our משנה is about a flame that bends low. But for a flame that shoots up high, even any small gap makes him exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and reads the משנה the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the משנה needs a whole public road to free him only when the flame is low, because that kind of fire spreads well. A high flame barely spreads sideways, so any small gap at all already makes him פטור. Both agree that a low flame spreads more easily. They disagree about which case the משנה's public-road rule is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
Exempt, does not have to pay

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
Our Mishnah is about a flame that bends low,
but for a flame that shoots up high,
even any small gap makes him exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מַתְנִיתִין בְּנִכְפֶּפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same משנה that רב explained in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is about a low flame. With a high flame, any gap at all exempts the person.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the exemption is for a high flame. A low flame that has wood to burn makes him liable even 100 מיל away. A river or pool eight אמות wide always exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught like רב: When is this said? With a flame that shoots up high. But with a low flame that has wood available to it, he is liable even up to a hundred מיל. If the fire crossed a river or a pool eight אמות wide, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רב, which supports his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא limits the exemption to a high flame, just as רב did. It even goes further for a low flame that has fuel: the person is liable up to 100 מיל, a much bigger distance than רב's 100 אמות. Water is different, though. A river or pool eight אמות wide stops any fire, so he is פטור either way.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him
When is this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)
A mil, a long distance of 2,000 אמות
A pool or puddle of water

steps.whyThisMatters: Because a ברייתא supports רב, his reading of the משנה gains strength over שמואל's.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in line with Rav:
When is this said?
With a flame that shoots up high,
but with a low flame that has wood available to it,
he is liable even up to a hundred mil.
If it crossed a river or a pool
that is eight cubits wide, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's side of the disagreement from steps 12 and 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the exemption applies only to a high flame
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that limits the exemption to a high flame and makes a low flame with fuel liable even 100 מיל away

steps.title: Who holds the public road rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'a public road' and asks which תנא holds that crossing one exempts the person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'A public road.' Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה and asks whose opinion they follow. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to know which named תנא agrees that a public road is wide enough to stop liability. This is a request for information, not an attack on the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

phrases.english: "A public road."
Who is the tanna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next phrase of the משנה from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a public road stops liability for a spreading fire

steps.title: רבא: It is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that this is רבי אליעזר, who uses sixteen אמות, the width of a public road, as the measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is רבי אליעזר. As we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says: Sixteen אמות, like a public road (he is exempt).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: the 'public road' rule matches רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר uses sixteen אמות as his measure, which is the width of a public road. So a fire that crosses a whole public road has gone past his limit, and the person is פטור. That fits our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sixteen cubits, the width of a public road

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer,
as we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Sixteen cubits,
like a public road (he is exempt).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'פטור'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who measures by sixteen אמות, the width of a public road.

steps.title: What kind of river does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's word 'river', רב says it means a real river. שמואל says it means a water channel used by people drawing water.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'Or a river.' רב says: an actual river. And שמואל says: a water channel of the water-drawers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's word 'river', and רב and שמואל disagree about what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'river' literally, as a real river. שמואל says even a smaller water channel, the kind used for drawing water to the fields, counts. In that case, even a smaller stretch of water is enough to make him פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel used by people who draw water

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's three barriers are each explained. A fence is measured from the thorn tops for a thorny field. A public road follows רבי אליעזר's sixteen אמות. For a river, רב says a real river and שמואל says even a water channel.

phrases.english: "Or a river."
Rav says: an actual river,
and Shmuel says: a water channel of the water-drawers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ נָהָר. רַב אָמַר: נָהָר מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next word of the משנה after 'public road'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב says the משנה means an actual river. שמואל says it means even a water channel.

steps.title: The practical difference between רב and שמואל: a dry river
steps.stepSummary: According to רב, a real river exempts even without water. According to שמואל, a water channel exempts only when it has water in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'a real river' means it counts even if there is no water in it. The one who says 'a channel used by water-drawers' means that if it has water in it, yes, it counts; but if it has no water in it, no, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what difference the argument from Step 17 makes in practice. It all depends on whether there is water inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real river is deep and wide, so even its dry bed is enough to stop a normal fire, and the person is פטור. A small channel only stops a fire because of the water in it. So when it is dry, the person is not פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel that people draw water from

steps.whatToRemember: רב: a real river exempts even when dry. שמואל: a small channel exempts only when it has water.

phrases.english: The one who says 'a real river'
phrases.notes: This is רב from the last step.

phrases.english: means it counts even though there is no water in it;
and the one who says 'a channel of the water-drawers'
if there is water in it, yes, it exempts,
but if there is no water in it, no, it does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר נְהַר מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical result of the רב / שמואל argument in Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A real river exempts even when dry; a water channel exempts only when it holds water.

steps.title: A משנה in פאה: things that divide a field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת פאה that lists things that split one field into separate fields for פאה, including a שלולית.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: These divide a field for פאה: a stream, a שלולית, a private road, and a public road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related משנה about פאה that also mentions streams and roads. This sets up the next question about the unclear word שלולית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A farmer leaves פאה once for each field. If something divides the field, each part counts as its own field and needs its own פאה. The list sounds like our משנה's river and road, which is why the גמרא brings it here.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
The corner of the field left for the poor
A water-related divider; its meaning is discussed next

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת פאה (2:1).

phrases.english: And these divide a field for פאה:
the stream, and the shelulit,
and a private road, and a public road.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the river in our משנה to a similar list in משנה פאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stream, a שלולית, a private road, and a public road divide a field for פאה.

steps.title: What is a שלולית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word שלולית in the פאה משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a שלולית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear word שלולית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stream and roads are clear, but שלולית is not. Before we know which things divide a field, we need to define this word.

phrases.english: What is a shelulit?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁלוּלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the משנה just quoted.

steps.title: Two definitions: gathered rainwater or a water channel
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says a שלולית is a place where rainwater gathers. רבי יוחנן says it is a water channel that spreads its water to the sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: it is a place where rainwater gathers. רב ביבי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is a water channel that hands out its 'spoils' to its sides.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different definitions of שלולית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל links the word to water that collects (שוללין). רבי יוחנן links it to שלל, 'spoils,' like a channel giving out its water to the land on its banks. One is a temporary puddle area; the other is a real channel.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
It is a place where rainwater gathers.
רב ביבי said that רבי יוחנן said:
It is a water channel that hands out 'spoils' to its sides.
phrases.notes: He means the channel spreads its water out to the land along its banks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל: a place where rainwater gathers. רבי יוחנן: a water channel that spreads water to its sides.

steps.title: What each definition includes and leaves out
steps.stepSummary: According to שמואל, a water channel certainly divides a field too. According to רבי יוחנן, only a channel divides, and a rainwater spot does not. The reason begins and continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is a place where rainwater gathers would all the more so say a water channel divides. But the one who says it is a water channel holds that a place where rainwater gathers does not divide, because these...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical difference between the two definitions. It starts giving רבי יוחנן's reason, and the sentence continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a spot of rainwater divides a field, then a real channel, which is stronger, surely does (כל שכן). But רבי יוחנן, who defined it as a channel, does not let a rainwater spot divide. The word 'because these' opens his reason, which comes next.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sentence is finished. 'דהנהו' starts רבי יוחנן's reason, and the rest comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְקוֹם שֶׁמֵּי גְשָׁמִים שׁוֹלְלִין שָׁם –
phrases.english: The one who says it is a place where rainwater gathers,
phrases.notes: This is שמואל from the last step.

phrases.english: all the more so a water channel divides;
but the one who says it is a water channel,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מְקוֹם שֶׁמֵּי גְשָׁמִים שׁוֹלְלִין שָׁם
phrases.english: holds that a place where rainwater gathers
does not divide, because these...

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְקוֹם שֶׁמֵּי גְשָׁמִים שׁוֹלְלִין שָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the practical difference between the two definitions in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל both a rainwater spot and a channel divide; according to רבי יוחנן only a channel divides.
